front: Define the centre of mass of a system of particles.
back: The mass-weighted average position: R = Σmᵢrᵢ/M (n particles), or X = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂)/(m₁+m₂) for two. Equal masses: CM midway.

front: Where is the CM of homogeneous regular bodies, and must it lie inside the body?
back: At the geometric centre by symmetry (reflection symmetry ×dm = 0). No — e.g. a ring or bangle has its CM in empty space at the centre.

front: How is the CM of a continuous body computed?
back: R = (1/M)∫r dm (6.5b); with the origin at the CM, ∫r dm = 0 (6.6).

front: What equation governs the motion of the centre of mass?
back: M A = F_ext (6.11): the CM moves as if the entire mass were concentrated there and all external forces acted there. Internal forces never affect the CM.

front: Total linear momentum of a system of particles?
back: P = Σmᵢvᵢ = M V (6.15); dP/dt = F_ext (6.17); if F_ext = 0 then P = constant and the CM moves uniformly (6.18a).

front: Define the vector (cross) product c = a × b.
back: Magnitude ab sinθ; direction perpendicular to the plane of a and b given by the right-handed screw (or right-hand curl) rule, through the smaller angle (< 180°).

front: List the essential properties of the cross product.
back: a×b = −b×a (non-commutative); distributive a×(b+c) = a×b + a×c; unchanged under mirror reflection; î×ĵ = k̂, ĵ×k̂ = î, k̂×î = ĵ (cyclic positive).

front: How are linear and angular velocity related in rotation, and when does v = ω × r apply?
back: vᵢ = ωrᵢ (6.19); vectorially v = ω × r (6.20) with r from an origin on the axis. It holds for any rotation with one point fixed (e.g. a spinning top).

front: Define angular acceleration.
back: α = dω/dt (6.21). For rotation about a fixed axis the direction of ω (and α) is fixed, so the equation reduces to its scalar form α = dω/dt (6.22).

front: Define torque (moment of force) and its magnitude.
back: τ = r × F (6.23); τ = rF sinθ = r⊥F = rF⊥ (6.24). Zero if the line of action passes through the origin. Vector, SI unit N m, dimensions ML²T⁻².

front: Define the angular momentum of a particle and relate its rate of change.
back: l = r × p (6.25a), magnitude l = rp sinθ (6.26). dl/dt = τ (6.27), the rotational analogue of F = dp/dt.

front: Angular momentum of a system of particles and the external-torque law.
back: L = Σ rᵢ×pᵢ (6.25b). With Newton's third law AND central forces, τ_int = 0, so dL/dt = τ_ext (6.28b); L = constant if τ_ext = 0 (6.29a).

front: What are the conditions for mechanical equilibrium of a rigid body?
back: ΣFᵢ = 0 (translational, 6.30a) and Στᵢ = 0 (rotational, 6.30b) — six scalar conditions; only three are needed for coplanar forces.

front: What is a couple, and what does it produce?
back: Two equal, opposite forces with different lines of action. Net force zero, net torque non-zero ⟹ pure rotation without translation. Its moment AB × F is origin-independent (Example 6.7).

front: State the principle of moments for a lever.
back: Load arm × load = effort arm × effort: d₁F₁ = d₂F₂ (6.32a). Mechanical advantage M.A. = F₁/F₂ = d₂/d₁ (6.32b).

front: Define the centre of gravity and its relation to the centre of mass.
back: The point where the total gravitational torque is zero: Σ rᵢ × mᵢg = 0 (6.33). With uniform g it coincides with the CM; in a varying field the two differ.

front: Define the moment of inertia and the rotational kinetic energy.
back: I = Σmᵢrᵢ² (6.34); K = ½Iω² (6.35). I is the rotational analogue of mass — a property of the body and the axis, independent of ω.

front: What is the radius of gyration k?
back: Defined by I = Mk²: the distance from the axis of a point mass of the body's total mass with the same moment of inertia. Rod about midpoint k = L/√12; disc about diameter k = R/2.

front: Recall Table 6.1: moments of inertia of regular bodies about given axes.
back: Ring MR² (centre) & MR²/2 (diameter); rod ML²/12 (midpoint); disc MR²/2 (centre) & MR²/4 (diameter); hollow cylinder MR²; solid cylinder MR²/2; solid sphere 2MR²/5.

front: Write the kinetic equations for rotation about a fixed axis.
back: ω = ω₀ + αt (6.36); θ = θ₀ + ω₀t + ½αt² (6.37); ω² = ω₀² + 2α(θ − θ₀) (6.38).

front: Work, power, and Newton's second law for rotation.
back: dW = τ dθ (6.39); P = τω (6.40); τ = Iα (6.41) — analogues of dW = F ds, P = Fv and F = ma.

front: Angular momentum for rotation about a fixed axis.
back: L_z = Iω k̂ (6.42b); for bodies symmetric about the axis L = Iω k̂ (6.42d). For asymmetric bodies L is not along the axis. L⊥ is constant.

front: State the conservation law for rotation about a fixed axis and give an example.
back: If τ_ext = 0, L_z = Iω = constant (6.44). Swivel chair: stretching the arms raises I and lowers ω; folding them raises ω. Acrobats, divers, skaters use it.
